paper.title: Characterizing the Effect of Noise in Language Generation in the Limit
paper.summary: Characterizes uniform and non-uniform generation under finitely many distinct noisy values, proves that every positive fixed finite noise level collapses to level one, separates noiseless generation from one-noise generation, and relates fixed-level and noise-dependent generation.

formalization_scope.summary: The custom inventory contains four headline theorems and four groups of core definitions. Lean fully covers all headline results and the enumeration, fixed-level, and noise-dependent interfaces; the noisy-closure card is partial only because the library represents dimension finiteness directly rather than defining a single extended-natural numerical value.
specializations: The generic wrappers make the source's countable nonempty universe and infinite-language assumptions explicit as Countable, Nonempty, and AllLanguagesInfinite hypotheses.
Theorem 2.17 is stated on the source's literal universe of pairs of natural numbers and uses the version of Algorithm 1 that retains rejected scan iterations.
Theorems 2.18 and 2.19 each package the source's three equivalent conditions together with an existential noiseless-versus-one-noise separation.
Finite noisy-closure dimension is represented by the exact finiteness predicate needed by the headline results rather than by a separately defined extended-natural numerical value.
The development is classical semantic mathematics and makes no extracted-executability, runtime, or query-complexity claim.
gaps: No P19 claim currently has a human correspondence audit; source assessment is based on the maintained PaperMap and AI-assisted comparison, while kernel checking verifies only the Lean declarations and their accepted axioms.

The supporting Lemmas 2.13 and 3.2 expose witness monotonicity, witness transfer, and finiteness consequences rather than literal inequalities between extended-natural-valued dimensions; this representational API gap does not weaken Theorems 2.16--2.19.

claims.title: Enumeration with at most i distinct noisy values
claims.statement_summary: An enumeration of an infinite target language K at noise level i is an injective infinite sequence whose range contains K and contains at most i distinct values outside K.

relations.notes: For injective streams, Lean proves that P19's bound on distinct off-target range values is equivalent to P06's bound on off-target occurrence indices; the generation success criteria remain different.

claims.title: Uniform and non-uniform generation at a fixed noise level
claims.statement_summary: At a fixed finite noise level i, one generator must eventually output fresh target elements on every level-i noisy enumeration. Uniform generation uses one stabilization time for the whole class, whereas non-uniform generation allows the time to depend on the target language but not on its enumeration.

claims.title: Uniform and non-uniform noise-dependent generation
claims.statement_summary: One generator must succeed at every finite noise level. In the uniform notion, the stabilization time may depend on the noise level but not on the target or enumeration; in the non-uniform notion it may additionally depend on the target, but not on the enumeration.

claims.title: Noisy consistency, closure, and noisy-closure dimension
claims.statement_summary: At level i, the languages consistent with an observed set S are those missing at most i elements of S. The noisy closure is their intersection, with the empty set used when no language is consistent. The noisy-closure dimension is the largest size of a finite S having a nonempty consistent family but finite noisy closure, or infinity when such witnesses are arbitrarily large.

source_assessment.notes: The empty-version-space convention is explicit in Definition 2.9.

formalization.notes: Lean directly represents consistency, closure, witnesses, and finiteness of the dimension, but does not define a single extended-natural-valued numerical dimension.

claims.title: All positive finite noise levels collapse to one
claims.statement_summary: For every class of infinite languages over a countable nonempty universe and every finite noise level i at least one, uniform generation at level i is equivalent to uniform generation at level one, and the corresponding non-uniform notions are also equivalent.

source_assessment.notes: The wrapper combines the source's uniform and non-uniform collapse clauses and keeps the positive-level hypothesis explicit.

claims.title: Noiseless uniform generation does not imply one-noise non-uniform generation
claims.statement_summary: There exists a class of infinite languages over pairs of natural numbers that is uniformly generatable from noiseless injective enumerations but is not non-uniformly generatable when one distinct extraneous value is allowed.

claims.title: Uniform noisy generation is characterized at level one
claims.statement_summary: For every class of infinite languages over a countable nonempty universe, finite level-one noisy-closure dimension is equivalent both to uniform generatability at every positive finite noise level and to uniform noise-dependent generatability; moreover, some noiselessly uniformly generatable class is not uniformly generatable at noise level one.

source_assessment.notes: Lean represents finiteness of noisy-closure dimension directly and preserves the source's equivalences and strict separation.
